SCWC_WarcasketHelmet_Shipcracker.descrip.english:
Specialized spacer-tech warcasket helmet with improved impact dispersion, sealed and equipped with an onboard respirator and an aiming assist.

10th generation warcaskets were actually adapted from captured pirate rigs, with government military research divisions improving them with advanced power armor designs. Access to a greater amount of high quality resources and the objective of equipping them onto combat veterans that would otherwise be unable to serve meant the program created single-user operated dreadnoughts. The versatility of the armors have been improved, generally reducing restrictions on mixing pieces of different armor series even across generations.

The Shipcracker series is an Imperial boarding pattern rather than a pirate one, built to cross the gap between two ships and open the far hull from the outside. Its drop thrusters throw the pilot across the vacuum onto the enemy hull, and the landing punches through into the interior. Under gravity the same burn clears a wall or a roof in a single hop. Because the shield only stops ranged attacks, this series is suited to pilots who prefer close work and expect to take a ship room by room. Salvage and desertion have since put the pattern in foundries far from any Imperial dock.
